discovery: Invention of the quantum cascade laser
subfield: Optics, laser physics and semiconductor quantum engineering
motivation: In 1994 Faist, Capasso and Cho demonstrated the quantum cascade laser. It was a new kind of light source whose emission wavelength comes from the design of quantum wells rather than from a material's natural bandgap. It relies on intersubband transitions in heterostructures grown by molecular beam epitaxy, a technique Cho pioneered. Through quantum engineering, it gave the mid-infrared and terahertz ranges compact, powerful and tunable coherent sources, opening up the molecular fingerprint region of the spectrum. QCLs and their frequency combs are now central to trace-gas sensing, environmental monitoring, industrial process control and biomedical spectroscopy, including diagnostics based on infrared molecular fingerprints. The invention is a model of curiosity-driven physics becoming a disruptive technology with large social benefit, and it has made visible molecular signals that could not be seen before.
